- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model overcorrects in next 3–5 days; reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-period, model fails to adjust; apply mean reversion to forecast 3–7 days ahead, averaging last 5–7 days’ true values.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates in high-sentiment periods; apply 1–3% downward bias if sentiment > 0.67 in last 5 days.  
- If sentiment is negative or neutral and true price drops >3% from recent peak, model often misses it; add 1–2% upward bias to prevent underestimation.
